questions.note: The risk was the opposite of order bias -- this was my v1 favourite and the pull was to protect its PASS -- so 5-7 were checked against pixels only, and TYPE and FAM rest on the licence file and the sheet.

findings.problem: /'s THE FRONTIER block is a two-column link pair list styled like the CATALOG and DEPRECATED blocks beside it, so the board's character never reaches the surface a first-time visitor lands on.
findings.invariant: The home Frontier block carries at least one board-specific property present on no other rail block: the two-weight lead pair plus the board's horizontal row rules.
findings.prescription: Not a re-file of the declined F-hier-2: keep the fixed two-column excerpt and no overflow container, and carry the row rules and .board-lead weight onto it.

findings.problem: .board-hatch is correct in CSS and unreachable in data: the claim cell falls back to any cited org fact, price/context/model are filled for all 16 matched orgs, and the index column is omitted whole.
findings.invariant: At least one hatched cell renders on /frontier on shipped data, at 1440 and 390, within the first viewport; or fixed copy states nothing is currently unstated.
findings.prescription: Drop the firstCitedFact(org) fallback; the blanks that appear are the move, and their count is the page's most interesting number.

findings.problem: Two of seven columns are unreadable at 1440: VENDOR CLAIM is cut mid-word for all 16 rows and the READ provenance cell that makes a row citable is entirely off-screen, with no visible scroll affordance.
findings.invariant: At 1440 no board cell's text is visually truncated and the per-row provenance cell is within the first viewport; scrolled columns carry a persistent visible edge affordance.
findings.prescription: Clamp the claim cell to an excerpt with its own ellipsis, and place the read date ahead of the claim.

findings.problem: VENDOR CLAIM labels sourced organisation founding facts as unverified vendor claims because the cell takes the first cited fact of any kind, which trains a reader to ignore the stamp.
findings.invariant: Every cell under VENDOR CLAIM is a claim the vendor made about that row's model, verbatim with source and accessed date; a record without one renders the labelled blank, never a substituted fact.
findings.prescription: Type the fact at the source instead of taking the first cited one, letting absence fall through to the labelled blank -- which also repairs F-sys-2-3.

findings.problem: Home's WHAT IT MEANS blocks set --step--1 prose across the ~90-character feed column, the widest measure at the smallest size on the sheet and the only visible break in the one-measure rule.
findings.invariant: No prose block on any template exceeds ~75 characters per line at --step--1 or smaller.
findings.prescription: Cap the annotation block at --measure inside the feed row rather than letting it inherit the column.

findings.problem: Every capture is theme-stamped (manifest theme: light|dark), so the un-stamped 'auto' state the contract asks about has no image in the evidence set.
findings.invariant: The evidence set contains a capture of /frontier and / with no data-theme attribute set, under each of prefers-color-scheme light and dark.
findings.prescription: Add an un-stamped pair to the rig's route matrix.

findings.problem: Whether a hatched cell reads as candour or as breakage is unanswered, and now carries F-sys-2-3's remedy, which deliberately introduces blanks onto the flagship.
findings.invariant: In the keeper reader test, no reader describes a hatched cell as broken, missing or an error when asked what it means.
findings.prescription: Carry the hatch into MR-UI-001 as a why-is-this-cell-striped question, on a build that renders one.

carried_forward.note: Resolved: Space Grotesk OFL 1.1, SpaceGrotesk-OFL.txt, 10,860 B and 10,300 B against the ~30 KB cap, declared on --mono.
Satisfied differently per discipline rule 4: the prose templates inherited the face through --mono, not board column tokens, and IR-CP-UI-001-2-1 states an 'unchanged, because' for each of the six.
Declined with cause (R6, R2) and accepted; F-sys-2-4 asks only for row rules and lead-pair weight on the existing fixed excerpt.
Superseded by F-sys-2-8: it now gates a remedy rather than a shipped state.

diagnosis.strongest: TYPE and FAM: heading the existing --mono token instead of forking one made a single edit carry Space Grotesk to all sixteen templates, with metric overrides so the swap costs no reflow.
diagnosis.weakest: ALLR on the shipped pixels: the bet -- absence drawn as plainly as presence -- sits in the CSS and reaches no cell, leaving a competent table on the flagship and the round-0 home in a new label face.
diagnosis.critical_issue: Question 5 moves PASS to FAIL against the anchor on an observable count: zero hatched cells across 112 in both themes and widths, and a home Frontier block that is a link list, not the board's rows.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Restrict the vendor-claim cell to actual vendor claims and drop the first-cited-fact fallback: one change repairs the mislabel, renders the hatched blank for the first time, and makes the blank count the flagship data statement.

downstream.weakness: The build shipped an identity (a face) without the gesture (the blank), and only the gesture answers K10's 'mechanical'.
downstream.cause: The empty state was written as a fallback for missing data rather than a typed condition, so a permissive fallback in the same cell consumed every case that would have triggered it.
downstream.recommendation: Add a rig assertion counting rendered .board-hatch cells on /frontier, and judge the next round's question 5 from home first.
